chapter: Working with Duke and final reflections
title: Meeting Duke and Sue at Robinson's Restaurant
summary: Whaley retells arriving in New York in 1921, meeting Duke at Robinson's Restaurant and meeting his wife Sue Baker, whom he married in 1927.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Now Tom, just in your own words about how you met Duke, in your association down through the years, please.

Well, I came to New York in '21, the last of November, and Robinson's restuarant was a big thing going then, at the corner of 131st Street and 7th Avenue, and all the performers used to go up there, see, and hang out there. Big Jones was at the corner, and Blackie's was around the corner there somewhere, and I'm in there playing the piano one night, and a guy said, "Here's Duke Ellington" and I kept on playing, and said, "Oh yeah?" and then they introduced me to Duke --and we became great friends through the years. And that's where I met my wife.
Yeah, well my wife and your wife were good friends.

Yeah. And I tell you, Sue came in this place and she had a blue dress on and she was beautiful, and I was playing the piano, and she came up and put her arms around me and I said, 'Take your arms around me!' and she said, 'I'm not married' and I said 'You're not married?' and she said, 'No' -- so I said to give me her telephone number and I would call her up tomorrow.

And I didn't call her up -- no, I called her up and a man answered, and I said, hell, she said she wasn't married. So when I saw her, I saw her walking down 7th Avenue one day and I said hello and told her that I called her up and she said that you weren't married, and your husband answered, and she said that it was her brother. I said, 'Yeah?'
You know, we got married in '27, and she died in '40 or '50 --she lived 20 years, we were married 20 years, rather. She died in '46 I think. She was an epileptic.
